label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
**To everyone on Aughrim Terrace,**

I’m putting this through every door because I don’t know who’s responsible, and I’m not going to point fingers at the wrong person. But whoever is putting their rubbish in my bin needs to stop.

It’s the grey Greenmount Bins bin belonging to No. 14, with **14 painted in white on the lid**. It goes out on Tuesday night for collection on Wednesday morning. It is not a communal bin.

For about a month now, somebody has been putting full black bags into it every week. Not the odd wrapper or a few bits — full bags of household rubbish. When I got home from work at 3am last Tuesday, there were three bags in it that weren’t mine, including one containing nappies. The lid wouldn’t even close.

Greenmount charges me by weight, at €0.41 a kilo. My last bill was **€63.20 for two months**, when it’s usually around €25. I’m absolutely fuming that I’m being left to pay for somebody else’s rubbish on top of my own.

I work nights. Coming home after a shift to find that someone has filled a bin I pay for is taking the piss. Having it out for collection is not an invitation to help yourself to the space, and me not being there to catch you doesn’t mean I’ll quietly put up with it.

If you’re stuck with getting your rubbish collected, ask. I’ll tell you who to ring. What you don’t do is quietly make it your neighbour’s problem and leave them with the bill.

I don’t want a row with anyone on the road. I want to be able to put my bin out without paying to get rid of someone else’s black bags. If it continues, I’ll be fitting a padlock.

To everyone who has nothing to do with this, sorry for the letter. To whoever does: you know those bags aren’t mine, and you know who’s paying for them.

**Stop putting them in my bin.**

**No. 14**
